description: Judge the complete standard transformer lineage, contribution summaries, and canvas notes.
criteria: Topic relevance and coverage: the seed is fixture:transformer; the graph includes fixture:seq2seq, fixture:alignment; excludes the unrelated distractor fixture:vgg. Do not demand exhaustive coverage beyond this bounded catalog.

Historical and scientific accuracy: generated paper summaries and notes agree with the reference facts, distinguish each method's contribution, and do not invent priority, experimental results, or guarantees. A generic standard-mode seed summary is acceptable only if notes explain the seed contribution.

Relationship accuracy: edges point from antecedent to later work, and explanatory text distinguishes cited evidence from conceptual inference. A verified citation alone is not proof of methodological dependence or exclusive invention; avoid overstating concurrent work as derivation.

Notes usefulness: 1 to 3 substantive canvas notes explain at least one concrete transition or dependency between the required foundational works and the seed, rather than merely listing titles or calling papers foundational.

Notes grounding: each note connects to all papers material to its explanation, without irrelevant connections, and supports its claims using the reference facts and supplied graph. No invented contributions or citations.

description: Judge a three-paper explanatory chain, including the transition to external retrieval.
concept: From sequence-to-sequence translation to retrieval-augmented generation
reference_facts: The Transformer cites seq2seq (reference 35); RAG cites the Transformer (reference 58). These graph links represent citations, not exclusive ancestry.
The conceptual chain moves from recurrent encoder-decoder sequence mapping to attention-based transduction, then supplements sequence generation with external retrieved memory.
criteria: At least one note explains both transitions across seq2seq, Transformer, and RAG, and connects to all three papers.

The notes correctly distinguish recurrent sequence mapping, attention without recurrence, and generation conditioned on retrieved documents; they do not credit seq2seq with attention or the Transformer with inventing retrieval.
All 1 to 3 notes add concrete explanatory value and contain no unsupported causal, experimental, or priority claims; connections match each note's actual claims.

description: Judge whether notes preserve uncertainty when only a conceptual relationship is supplied.
reference_facts: REALM learns retrieval in language-model pretraining; RAG combines dense retrieval with sequence generation.

For this case the graph deliberately supplies ONLY a conceptual relationship, with no verified reference evidence. Do not infer direct citation or derivation from the graph, even if the judge knows the papers externally.
criteria: At least one note explains the distinction between retrieval-augmented pretraining in REALM and sequence generation with retrieved evidence in RAG, connecting to both papers.
The notes treat the edge as conceptual or explicitly uncertain, never claiming the supplied graph proves direct citation, derivation, or that RAG uses REALM as its retriever.
All 1 to 3 notes stay within the provided evidence, with no invented comparative scores or assertions that retrieval eliminates hallucination.
